test_title: PYST 25: SSC CHSL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 09 Jul, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A person saves 45% of his income. Next year, his income increases by 200%. He increases his savings by five times the previous year’s savings. By what percentage (correct to one place of decimal) has he increased/decreased his expenditure?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Income** be 100, so **Savings** = 45 and **Expenditure** = 55.

New **Income** = 100 + 200 = 300.

New **Savings** = 5 × 45 = 225.

New **Expenditure** = 300 − 225 = 75.

% Increase in **Expenditure** = (75 − 55) / 55 × 100 = 20 / 55 × 100 ≈ 36.4%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increased, 36.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Savings** = 45% of **Income**

**Income** increase = 200%

Final **Savings** = 5 × Initial **Savings**

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

Percentage Change = (Final − Initial) / Initial × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6808f5618c1a6a24e96fd9462b6c4b02108e2c52ff947e9e5ee63ead8c21d3fe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Initial **Income** = 100

⇒ Initial **Savings** (S₁) = 45% of 100 = 45

⇒ Initial **Expenditure** (E₁) = 100 − 45 = 55

⇒ New **Income** (I₂) = 100 + (200% of 100) = 100 + 200 = 300

⇒ New **Savings** (S₂) = 5 × 45 = 225

⇒ New **Expenditure** (E₂) = 300 − 225 = 75

⇒ Increase in **Expenditure** = 75 − 55 = 20

⇒ Percentage Increase = (20 / 55) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 400 / 11 ≈ 36.36% ≈ 36.4%

**∴ The correct answer is Increased, 36.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

The fundamental relation is **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**. Any change in one variable must be balanced by the others.

Percentage Increase vs "Increase by X times"

An increase of 200% means the new value is 300% of the original (Multiplier = 3). "Increases by 5 times" can sometimes be interpreted as the new value being 5 times the old one or adding 5 times the old value to itself.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%, though in **Income-Expenditure** problems, simple linear addition of components is used.</p
